children: Tesla
has reclaimed more than half of the U.S. electric-vehicle market as traditional automakers scale back their money-losing EV operations.
The company captured 52% of U.S. EV sales through August, up from 43% a year earlier, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing data from Motor Intelligence. The gain reflects Tesla’s
relative resilience rather than a return to growth. Its domestic sales fell 16% to 325,351 vehicles while the overall EV market contracted 30%.
For investors, Tesla’s

rising share strengthens its competitive position but doesn't resolve weakening demand. The company is taking a larger slice of a shrinking market, with much of its automotive business dependent on the Model Y. Longer-term returns increasingly hinge on whether Tesla
can turn its investments in autonomous driving, artificial intelligence and robotics into meaningful revenue.
Tesla’s

market share had fallen to a record-low 41% in 2025 as competitors introduced more electric models and Chief Executive Elon Musk’s political activities alienated some buyers. Its recovery has coincided with Ford
, General Motors
and other automakers reducing production or discontinuing EVs after federal incentives expired.

The Honda Prologue, Volkswagen ID.4 and Ford F-150 Lightning are among the models being eliminated or phased out. GM also reduced production plans for the revived Chevrolet Bolt while Nissan delayed the least-expensive version of its new Leaf.
Tesla’s
Model Y remains the company’s main defense against the downturn. Sales declined only 2% this year and the SUV accounted for roughly one-third of all U.S. EV purchases. Tesla
also introduced a longer, six-seat Model Y L this summer.
Other models have struggled. Model 3 sales dropped 34% while Tesla
sold only 9,769 Cybertrucks. The company also discontinued the Model S and Model X without direct replacements as Musk shifted attention toward robotaxis and humanoid robots.
Analysts expect Tesla

to retain its dominant U.S. position while established automakers remain cautious about EV investment, the Journal reported. A stronger competitive challenge may require cheaper battery technology, renewed regulatory support or a significant improvement in consumer demand.

title: Tesla regains majority of U.S. EV market as rivals retreat: WSJ
